title: What to know about the Green Line shutdowns planned for August
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: The MBTA Green Line will undergo service changes in August for tunnel upgrades and accessibility improvements.
Free shuttle buses will replace Green Line service on affected branches, adding an estimated 25 minutes to commutes.
Symphony Station remains closed for upgrades until spring 2029; specific C branch stops will close temporarily in August.

title: Suffolk corrections officer killed after stopping to help stranded motorist in Boxford
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Brett Martin, 51, a Suffolk corrections officer, died after being struck by a vehicle while helping a motorist on I-95.
The incident occurred on Monday evening in Boxford; Martin was taken to a hospital and later pronounced dead.
Massachusetts State Police and the Essex County District Attorney's Office are investigating the fatal accident.

title: Review & setlist: Tame Impala reimagines the bounds of arena rock at TD Garden
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Tame Impala performed two sold-out shows at TD Garden, showcasing their evolution from small venues to large arenas.
The concert featured a 360-degree stage setup and included hits from various albums, like 'Lonerism' and 'Currents'.
Opener Djo, fronted by Joe Keery, engaged the crowd with songs from his 2025 album 'The Crux'.

title: Electric utility rates are going up Aug. 1. Will your bill actually increase?
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts electric rates will rise on Aug. 1 for National Grid, Eversource, and Unitil customers due to a supply rate reset.
Eversource basic service rates will increase from 15.6 to 17.3 cents per kWh; National Grid's variable rate goes to 16.074 cents.
Only 26.6% of Massachusetts customers on basic service will face the rate hike; others use municipal aggregation or competitive suppliers.

title: Man called in bomb threat after getting kicked out of Boston movie theater, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Christopher McFadden, 55, was arrested for a bomb threat at AMC theater on Tremont Street, Boston.
McFadden allegedly made threats after being removed for harassing a theater employee and threatening a manager.
Police linked McFadden to the threat through a cellphone found in his possession, confirming the call origin.

title: In new ‘milestone,’ Rhode Island nonprofit tags first hammerhead shark
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: The Atlantic Shark Institute in Rhode Island tagged its first hammerhead shark near Block Island.
The tagging will allow scientists to track the shark's movements along the East Coast for over a decade.
The event was filmed for an upcoming episode of 'Ocean State: Rhode Island's Wild Coast' documentary series.

title: Panera is moving its headquarters to this Boston suburb
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Panera is relocating its headquarters to Weston, Massachusetts, by July 2027, under the leadership of CEO Paul Carbone.
The St. Louis support center will remain, but many roles will transfer to Weston as part of the headquarters move.
Panera's move is part of the "Panera Rise" strategy, aiming to refresh its menu and expand its network.

title: How new MBTA pilot programs aim to save riders money
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Governor Maura Healey announced new MBTA pilot programs to make public transportation more affordable and accessible.
One program expands a 2-hour transfer window allowing unlimited transfers between subway, bus, and ferry at the highest fare.
Free fares will be offered to seniors 75 and older who no longer drive, with details announced in the fall.

title: Two Concord residents die in head-on crash
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: John and Paula Hamilton, aged 82 and 85, died in a head-on collision in Concord on Saturday.
The crash occurred on Walden Street when a Honda crossed the center line and collided with a Tesla.
Three other individuals, including two Tesla passengers and the Honda driver, were hospitalized with injuries.

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with ex-husband expected back on the stand
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Patrick Clancy, ex-husband of Lindsay Clancy, to testify again in murder trial of their three children.
Lindsay Clancy uses an insanity defense, claiming postpartum mental illness influenced her actions in January 2023.
Prosecutors argue Lindsay Clancy acted intentionally, while defense blames psychiatric medications for her mental state.
